scoring: p_met is the chance that the trial meets its primary objective, given that a result is public by the deadline (2027-06-30): reported success under the round's labelling rules (a trial only vague at the deadline counts as not met; their number, and every score without them, are shown). Ranked result: the first pass, on the trials whose first public result comes after the close (2026-11-15) and on or before the deadline; earlier results are dropped and listed, trials still silent are dropped and counted. Two boards: Models (one model, the round's instructions (forecast_instructions.md, SHA-256 in this manifest) and the packet only: no web, no tools, no other model, one answer per trial, as declared by the entrant) and Open (anything else). Once 100 trials are scored, every entry is placed in one of three tiers against the registry model (ref-b1): clearly better (a Brier score of p_met lower by more than 0.005), no clear difference, or clearly worse (higher by more than 0.005). Each entry is tested on its own, so other entries cannot move its tier: two one-sided tests fixed in advance, from the standard deviation of a paired bootstrap that resamples sister-trial groups (sisters.json) together and a normal approximation; the smaller p-value is doubled and compared with 5%. Each board lists its entries by tier, then by Brier score (calibration counts, as in any proper score); comparisons between entries are shown as exploratory, never ranked. Shown with each entry, never ranked: whether it adds to the registry model (exploratory: the Brier gain of a logistic combination of logit(ref-b1) and logit(entry) over ref-b1 recalibrated alone, both fitted out of fold in 10 folds of whole sister groups, averaged over 5 splits, with an interval from 500 resamples that run the same estimator; it adds only if the interval is above 0 and the entry's weight is positive); its first upload's score next to its last, with both setups, when uploaded more than once. The organiser's model runs are on the Models board; the base rate (ref-b0) and the registry model (ref-b1), both matched to each trial's reporting window and published from the opening day, are shown as baselines. Skill against both with paired intervals; AUROC, reliability, resolution and the level gap shown. Optional rationale and evidence are published with the entries as plain text, never scored. An early pass with results up to 2027-03-31 (p_met_mar where given, else p_met; B0 and B1 worked out for that date) shows tiers once enough trials are scored there, as an early look, never the ranking. A supplementary pass with results up to 2027-12-31 (p_met_dec where given, else p_met) is shown, never ranked. Number questions: low80, median and high80 are the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles, all three scored with the percentile loss (the interval score of the 80% range plus 5 times the median's distance from the result), divided by the width of the frozen reference entry's (ref-opus-5-5) range, never less than a floor per question (10th percentile of comparable reference widths); summarised by the plain mean, with the median and the 5%-trimmed mean shown; void when the number is not published. Subgroup answers: scored the same way, shown, never ranked. The number score is ranked too: in the first pass, once 100 number questions are scored, each entry with number answers gets a number tier against ref-opus-5-5 (a number score lower or higher by more than 0.05), with the same test. Safety answers (the % stopping treatment for an adverse event, per arm) get the same percentile loss in percentage points; p_key_secondary and p_next_step their Brier score against the share in the round; assumptions the share their sources support; all shown, never ranked. Operations questions (p_late, p_stopped, p_posted): answered from the registry records as they stand on 2027-08-31; their own Brier score, against the share in the round itself, shown next to the ranking and never part of it. p_public (every trial with p_met; its own all-or-none block): the chance that a statement on the primary result comes out by 2027-06-30, so that p_met is scored, decided by the labellers from the first pass's labels; void when it came before the close; its own Brier score, and the Brier score of p_met x p_public against a statement by the deadline and met; neither part of the ranking. p_public_mar and p_public_dec: the same by the early and final deadlines, each its own block, with p_public_mar <= p_public <= p_public_dec. p_amended (every trial, its own block): the chance that the record's primary outcomes change in substance by the read date, judged by two labellers who compare the record as pulled for the round with the record fetched on the read date.
